option_relations.rationale: Necrotizing fasciitis is a severe bacterial infection of the fascia, not primarily characterized by ear necrosis as described.
While the patient has bacteremia, the description of ear lesions with full-thickness necrosis and sparse inflammation is more specific than general septic emboli with skin necrosis.
Necrotizing cellulitis is a severe form of cellulitis, but the biopsy findings of full-thickness necrosis of epidermis, dermis, and adnexal structures are more characteristic of ecthyma gangrenosum.
The vignette explicitly states 'No devices had been used on the ears,' ruling out pressure necrosis.
